context.body: This passage states that Israel lived in Egypt for four hundred thirty years and left at the end of that period.
context.label: The stated duration

observations.body: The firstborn deaths are described from Pharaoh’s throne to the captive in the dungeon and include livestock.
observations.label: From throne to dungeon

observations.body: Pharaoh rises, calls Moses and Aaron, and tells Israel to leave and serve the LORD.
observations.label: A night summons

observations.body: Egypt urges departure; Israel carries dough before it is leavened and later bakes it because they could not wait.
observations.label: Urgency and dough

observations.body: The passage names men on foot, children, a mixed multitude, flocks, herds, and livestock moving from Rameses to Succoth.
observations.label: A mixed company moves

observations.body: The closing line calls this a night to be observed by Israel throughout their generations.
observations.label: A watched night

payload.posture: Follow death, cry, summons, urgency, dough, movement, duration, and the remembered watch through the night.
payload.tension: Death and a great cry fill the night that also becomes the moment of summons, urgency, departure, and continuing memory.
payload.title: Midnight becomes departure
